games.name: Maneater
games.summary: Unreal Engine 4.25, Direct3D 11, Denuvo Anti-Tamper. Hangs on the spinning-shark loading screen under FEX with stock settings.
notes: v2 profile, after the first one still hung on the spinning-shark screen. It changes three things at once:

1. Audio: Maneater now uses DroidDeck's PulseAudio path with 100 ms latency (WINE_AUDIO_DRIVER=pulse, PULSE_LATENCY_MSEC=100) instead of DirectAudio. A ProtonDB report of this exact hang, after the first loading screen, was fixed with PULSE_LATENCY_MSEC=100, and DroidDeck's maintainers document the PulseAudio path as the fallback for audio problems.

2. Threads: all of FEX's memory-ordering emulation (TSO) is on, plus full x87 precision. Unreal's loading screen keeps animating while a background thread does the loading, and without strict ordering under translation that handoff can stall forever. This is slower than the first profile.
3. Unreal's async loading thread is turned off in Engine.ini, so loading happens on the main thread and that handoff never happens.
Kept from v1: full self-modifying-code checks and a hidden hypervisor bit for Denuvo, the OpenSSL CPU-feature fix, skipped intro movies and the handheld Engine.ini tweaks.
Be online for the first launch (Denuvo activation), and give the first load 5 to 10 minutes while FEX and DXVK warm their caches.
Denuvo can lock the game for 24 hours after about 5 hardware changes. Every profile here reports the same CPU, so switching between them should not count.

If it still hangs: in DroidDeck, Setup > Developer, turn on Session logs and Game debug logs, launch Maneater once, wait about 5 minutes at the shark, then Share logs. The Proton log shows exactly where it stops.

tweaks.name: Skip intro movies
tweaks.description: Renames the logo MP4s in Maneater/Content/Movies, so the game does not have to play video through Media Foundation at boot. They are renamed, not deleted, and revert puts them back.

tweaks.name: Handheld performance tweaks (Engine.ini)
tweaks.description: Turns off motion blur, depth of field, chromatic aberration and lens flares, and lowers volumetric fog. That is cheaper on the Adreno 740 and makes fewer shaders to build on first load.

tweaks.name: Unreal async loading thread off (loading-hang fix)
tweaks.description: Loads game packages on the main thread instead of a separate loading thread. Loading is a bit slower, but it removes the cross-thread handoff that can deadlock under x86 translation and leave the loading screen spinning forever.

profile.name: Best compatibility + performance
profile.description: Full memory-ordering emulation (TSO) and full code checks for Denuvo, PulseAudio with 100 ms latency instead of DirectAudio, and Unreal's async loading thread off. All three target the endless spinning-shark loading screen.

ui.name: UI scale 125%
ui.description: Sets Unreal Engine's ApplicationScale to 1.25 in Engine.ini. That scales every menu, HUD element and subtitle by 25% on top of the engine's own DPI scaling. Values much higher can push HUD elements off the edges.

games.name: Monster Hunter: World
games.summary: MT Framework, Direct3D 11/12, no Denuvo since June 2021. Very CPU-heavy, so x86 translation is the main bottleneck on the Thor.
notes: FEX uses DroidDeck's Performance + TSO preset. MT Framework spreads work over many threads, and without main TSO they can deadlock or corrupt state under translation. Vector and memcpy TSO stay off, and multiblock stays on, for speed.
DirectX 12 is turned off so the game runs through DXVK. ProtonDB players report DX11 on Proton is clearly faster than DX12, and DXVK is the most mature path on Turnip.

graphics_option.ini is set to 1280x720 at a 30 fps cap with the heavy effects off: volumetrics, SSR, water reflection, subsurface scattering, AO, snow, motion blur and depth of field. FidelityFX CAS sharpens the 720p image. The game writes this file on its first launch, so if it's missing, launch once, quit, and apply again.
If the game says a DX11 call is invalid after a Steam Cloud sync from a Windows PC, use 'Restore Default Settings' in the game's display options once, then apply here again.
The first hunt in a new area can stutter while DXVK builds shaders. It smooths out after that.
You can raise the frame cap later in Display settings (FrameRate=60), but under FEX the CPU usually can't hold 60 in towns or big fights.

profile.name: Best compatibility + performance
profile.description: FEX Performance + TSO, DX11 through DXVK, and a handheld 720p/30 graphics profile.

ui.name: UI scale (in-game only)
ui.description: Monster Hunter: World has no UI scale setting that can be changed from outside the game.
ui.manual:
Monster Hunter: World has no UI or font scale in its config files. Its text and HUD size settings live inside the encrypted save, which this app won't touch, and its Steam Deck patch (15.20) added no UI changes. To make it easier to read on the Thor:

• Start menu > Options > Game Settings > Text Size: set it to the largest size (subtitles and dialogue).
• Options > Display: raise the HUD-related sizes where offered.
• The Best settings button already sets 720p, which keeps the UI proportionally the same size but makes the game easier to run.

games.name: HITMAN World of Assassination
games.summary: Glacier 2, Direct3D 12 only (runs through VKD3D-Proton), no Denuvo. Has a separate launcher, and ray tracing is the main cause of freezes under Proton.
notes: -skip_launcher goes straight into the game. On Proton the IOI launcher often fails, or doesn't take controller input, and several ProtonDB players say the game would not start without it.
VKD3D_CONFIG=nodxr hides DirectX Raytracing from the game. ProtonDB reports consistently tie freezes within minutes of starting a mission to ray tracing, and the Adreno 740 can't afford it anyway.

VKD3D_FEATURE_LEVEL=12_1 goes with nodxr. DroidDeck issue #1293 shows HITMAN still crashes at startup when an older DroidDeck setup forces feature level 12_2, which advertises ray tracing the Adreno GPU can't run. 12_1 keeps it hidden.

VKD3D_FRAME_RATE=30 caps the game at a steady 30 fps. Several players found that capping the frame rate cut down hard freezes on loads and picture-in-picture, and under FEX the Thor won't hold much more in big levels like Marrakesh or Mumbai. Remove it in DroidDeck's Game environment if you want to experiment.
FEX uses DroidDeck's Performance + TSO preset. Glacier is heavily multithreaded and needs main TSO to avoid deadlocks.

Render scale is set to 75% through the game's SuperSampling registry value. This only works after the game has run once, so launch once, quit, and apply again if the log says the value isn't set yet. Changing graphics in the game can reset it.
Set graphics to Low or Medium in the game's options, with ray tracing off and no frame generation. The first mission load compiles shaders and takes a while.
Progression needs IOI's servers. If you get disconnected mid-mission, use Retry. Offline saves are separate from online ones.
Known, unsolved in DroidDeck (#1293): in the Guided Training tutorial, the 'Hold A to disguise yourself' step can ignore input forever. If it happens, skip the tutorial or restart the mission.

profile.name: Best compatibility + performance
profile.description: FEX Performance + TSO, ray tracing hidden at feature level 12_1, 30 fps cap, launcher skipped, 75% render scale.

ui.name: Handheld UI (Steam Deck mode)
ui.description: Sets SteamDeck=1 for this game. HITMAN has a built-in small-display mode for handhelds: interaction prompts twice the default size, larger HUD and menu text (24 vs 12, 22 vs 14), and action prompts, objectives and waypoints scaled ×1.2–1.5. Side effects: the game may show Steam Deck button prompts, and Steam's on-screen keyboard can pop up in text fields.

games.name: Dead Rising 2
games.summary: Forge engine, 32-bit Direct3D 9 (DXVK), no DRM beyond Steam. Runs well on the Thor's GPU; the problems are audio crackling, controller detection and framerate-tied gameplay.
notes: FEX uses DroidDeck's Performance + TSO preset. The game is light, but its multithreaded engine needs main TSO to avoid stalls under translation.

Audio: crackling is the most common Dead Rising complaint under Proton, and the Thor's Android audio output doesn't run in low-latency mode. This profile gives DroidDeck's DirectAudio a bigger buffer for this game only (AUDIO_DIRECT_MS=100, AUDIO_DIRECT_PERIOD_MS=25, up from 60 and 20). That adds about 40 ms of audio delay in exchange for no underruns. If it still crackles, DroidDeck's documented fallback is the PulseAudio path: in DroidDeck's Game environment for this game, add WINE_AUDIO_DRIVER=pulse and PULSE_LATENCY_MSEC=60.

The frame rate is capped at 60 through DXVK (d3d9.maxFrameRate = 60). The engine allows up to 120 FPS, but some gameplay, like pushable items and weapon ammo drain, runs too fast above 60, and the cap leaves CPU time for the audio thread.

Controller: the game only detects an official Xbox 360 pad, which is why DroidDeck reports it 'runs well but ignores the controller' (#386). The Controller fix button installs ClownDR2Fix v1.5.0.1, which switches the game to SDL's gamepad support. After applying, open Options > PC Settings in the game once and enable the controller if it's off.

An older DXVK isn't pinned. No source ties it to this crackling, and ClownDR2Fix's author warns that older Proton/DXVK versions corrupt its graphics fixes. If the audio fix isn't enough, DroidDeck's Components page can try DXVK 2.7.1 for this game alone.

profile.name: Best compatibility + performance
profile.description: FEX Performance + TSO, a larger DirectAudio buffer against crackling, and a 60 fps cap through DXVK.

ui.name: UI scale (in-game only)
ui.description: Dead Rising 2 has no UI scale setting.
ui.manual:
Dead Rising 2 has no UI or text scale setting, in its menus or its rendersettings.ini, and its HUD is laid out for 16:9 at any resolution. ClownDR2Fix only enlarges fonts above 1200p, which doesn't help at the Thor's 1080p. What helps:

• Options > Display: turn subtitles on.
• The Best settings button already caps the game at 60 fps, which keeps the HUD from stuttering.

extras.name: Controller fix (ClownDR2Fix)
extras.description: Downloads ClownDR2Fix v1.5.0.1 from its author's GitHub release (github.com/Clownacy/ClownDR2Fix), checks its SHA-256, and copies its 4 files into the game folder: dinput8.dll (ASI loader), DR2Fix.asi and two shader archives. It makes any controller work through SDL and fixes framerate-tied gameplay, the PC port's washed-out gamma and exposure, and the logo screens. No game file is replaced, and revert deletes exactly what was added. It also tells Wine to load the mod's dinput8.dll (WINEDLLOVERRIDES=dinput8=n,b) for this game only.

tweaks.name: ClownDR2Fix v1.5.0.1 (downloaded from GitHub, SHA-256 checked)

games.name: Disgaea 2 PC
games.summary: OpenGL 3.0, with separate Windows and Linux builds that read controllers differently.
notes: Controller: in the developer's own Steam layout, the Linux build uses Steam's 'SteamOS or Mac' game actions and the Windows build uses an ordinary Xbox pad. ProtonDB players report the Linux build losing controllers, and one fixed it by forcing Proton.

Why turning Steam Input off didn't help: DroidDeck's default pad is a Steam Deck controller, which normally becomes an Xbox pad only through Steam Input. This profile turns it on and picks Steam's stock gamepad layout. No keys are mapped.
After applying, start Steam in DroidDeck. If the Linux build was installed, Steam downloads the Windows files. Let that finish before launching.

Don't pick another layout or turn Steam Input off for this game. Steam can also sync an old layout back from the cloud; if input stops, choose the 'Gamepad' template in the game's controller settings.
If the game doesn't launch, choose another Proton for it on DroidDeck's Components page. One ProtonDB player needed 8.0-5 on a Steam Deck.

profile.name: Best compatibility + performance
profile.description: Runs the Windows build through Proton with Steam Input on and the stock gamepad layout, so the game should see an Xbox controller. FEX uses Performance + TSO.

tweaks.name: Use the Windows build (DroidDeck's default Proton)

ui.name: UI scale (in-game only)
ui.manual: No UI or text scale setting was found for Disgaea 2 PC outside the game. Valve's Steam Deck test lists its interface text as legible.
